events.summary: A further batch of 104 imported Metro Transit buses arrived in Sri Lanka.
US and Sri Lankan health authorities launched a dengue prevention and response programme.
President instructed officials to prepare a land scheme for returning overseas workers.
The 2026 budget allocated funds for replanting small tea estates.
Officials reported cumulative spending on small tea estate replanting.
Officials reviewed progress of 2026 human-elephant conflict projects and were directed to complete works promptly.
President instructed officials to protect northern and eastern coasts and curb illegal construction.
Government is adapting official residences for commercial or other public uses.
Kesbewa Council launched 4G camera monitoring to identify illegal dumpers.
Government is considering reinstating fuel subsidies to hold current petrol and diesel prices.
President directed officials to resolve the proposed overseas-worker pension scheme and include it in budget proposals.
President directed officials to promote three islands as green energy islands through the ongoing hybrid renewable energy project.
Government is implementing a national agricultural cooperative modernisation programme.
Government increased Cyclone Ditwah farmer compensation to Rs. 10,000 per acre.
Government allocated Rs. 16 billion for paddy purchases and began procurement.
Rs. 500 million allocated for modern paddy storage at 50 cooperatives.
Pallekele prison construction was completed.
Temporary accommodation construction at several prisons neared completion.
A high-security prison was established at Welisara Naval Camp.
Further prison development projects are planned for 2026 through 2029.
Nineteen investor proposals were opened for commercial activities at Mattala Airport.
Civil Aviation Authority plans a pilot passenger drone service.
Free confidential mobile clinics operate in Colombo and Gampaha to detect infections.
Cabinet extended monthly rent allowances for displaced households by three months.
Paddy Marketing Board began purchasing small-season paddy in Kilinochchi at stated kilo rates.
Government plans 500 tea villages, with 144 villages scheduled to begin in 2026.
Sri Lanka and India signed an agreement to obtain medical equipment for the new Deniyaya hospital.
Officials opened 19 proposals for commercial investment in Mattala airport operations.
Deputy minister promised a permanent housing solution for six families evicted in Ragala.
Minister directed officials to expedite surveying government and private land at the former brickworks.
Scholarships were handed to 114 students in Trincomalee under the nationwide programme.
Officials planned an Indian-assisted children’s park and computer centre for Ginigathhena.
Cabinet approved a pilot cluster bus company system using routes 177, 170 and 190.
Ministry extended applications for Asithisi journalism and technical scholarship schemes.
Tambuttegama water supply project, built with Chinese concessional lending and government funds, was completed.
Domestic donations received into the Treasury disaster fund for future recovery needs.
Foreign donations received into the Treasury disaster fund for future recovery needs.
Minister directed officials to provide special rail services during the Nallur festival.
JICA-funded second terminal construction is scheduled to resume in mid-November.
Modernisation and expansion work has begun at Jaffna International Airport.
Government is selecting investors for a public-private commercial development at Mattala Airport.
Rehabilitation of the Palaly military hospital was estimated at 99.3 million rupees.
55 million rupees has been spent on Palaly military hospital rehabilitation.
42.11 million rupees was allocated for Palaly military hospital rehabilitation this year.
A new air situation display system was installed at Jaffna International Airport.
Government indicated the LRT project was economically unviable and considered Metro Bus alternatives.
Jaffna District scheduled a special dengue control and awareness week for July 13–15.
Cabinet arranged funding for a CT scanner at Mannar District General Hospital.
President's Fund introduced a one-time education assistance scheme for students with disabilities at state universities.
The scheme will provide a one-time Rs. 100,000 education grant to each eligible student.
Minister signed an order establishing a new prison at Mahamodara.
IMF agreed to continue technical and advisory assistance for revenue administration reforms.
Railways restricted Kankesanthurai–Colombo daily service to four days weekly due to coach shortages.
National Tax Week began nationwide as part of the Badu Shakthi tax awareness programme.
National dengue elimination programme continued its second day with awareness and cleanup activities.
Narahenpita station modernisation was completed and returned to public use.
India funded construction of 57 permanent homes for landslide-risk families.
Sri Lanka allocated infrastructure funding for 57 homes in Phase Four.
Foundation stone laid for a new fuel station serving Neduntheevu residents.
Neduntheevu Maveli–Periyathurai road improvement work was inaugurated.
Health Ministry began a nationwide accident-prevention awareness week through July 10.
Joint dengue-control operations began across 23 high-risk zones in Western Province.
Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for a new three-storey school building.
Tank rehabilitation began using an MP’s decentralized development allocation.
Foundation stone laid for a new classroom building under the Northern Province education programme.
Cabinet approved the annual bus fare revision, with minimum fare set at Rs. 34.
Revised bus fares took effect, setting the minimum fare at Rs. 34.
June Aswesuma allowances released for elderly beneficiaries in both phases.
India-funded hybrid renewable power construction is nearing completion on Neduntheevu and nearby islands.
Construction of 1,300 homes in India’s 10,000-home estate housing project is nearing completion.
Government began coordinated interventions and plans awareness programmes to prevent HIV and sexually transmitted infections among students.
Government continued the diesel subsidy for July.
Cabinet approved transferring Horana District General Hospital to the central government.
World Bank announced $150 million for Sri Lanka's reform programme.
Railway Department temporarily suspended two Kelani Valley services pending further notice.
Cabinet approved the 2027 school footwear programme, including Rs. 3,000 vouchers per eligible student.
Officials discussed advancing the proposed Temple City tourism and cultural development project.
Two digitally enabled Sisu Sariya school bus services began in Jaffna.
Government launched the national Ceylon Tea Village programme in June.
Kalubowila Hospital received three modern treatment units costing over Rs. 555 million.
Treasury, ADB and JICA will fund nationwide expansion of cath lab units.
